'''Perla Sousi''' (born 1984){{r|cv}} is a Greek mathematician specialising in [[probability theory]], a professor in the Department of Pure Mathematics and Mathematical Statistics (DPMSS) at the [[University of Cambridge]], and a Fellow of [[Emmanuel College, Cambridge]].{{r|promo}}

==Education and career==
Sousi was born in 1984 in Athens. After a 2005 bachelor's degree in mathematics from the [[University of Patras]], she first came to the University of Cambridge in 2006 for [[Part III of the Mathematical Tripos]]. After study in 2006 and 2007 in France at the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)]] and the [[French Institute for Research in Computer Science and Automation]] (Inria), she completed her Ph.D. at Cambridge in 2011.{{r|cv}} Her dissertation, ''Collisions and detection for random walks and Brownian motion'', was supervised by [[James R. Norris]].{{r|mg}}

She continued at Cambridge as a Junior Research Fellow of Emmanuel College from 2011 to 2014, while also doing postdoctoral research in 2012 at the [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]] in [[Berkeley, California]]. She became a Fellow of Emmanuel College and a research associate of DPMMS in 2014.{{r|cv}} A readership at Cambridge was established in 2019,{{r|reader}} and she was made a full professor in 2024.{{r|promo}}

==Recognition==
Sousi received a 2025 [[Whitehead Prize]] "for her innovative contributions to the study of mixing and cutoff phenomena for Markov chains; to the study of random walks and Brownian motion in fixed and changing environments; and to the development of the potential theory of branching random walks on d-dimensional lattices".{{r|whitehead}}
